rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO) - Just Cause Requirements
rules.quote: If you own rental property in the City of Los Angeles, it may be subject to the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO). It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.summary: The Just Cause Ordinance prohibits landlords from terminating tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.coverage_text: In order to apply to a tenancy, it requires that the tenant either has lived in the same unit for at least six months or that their original lease expired, whichever comes first.
rules.exemption_note: Exceptions include transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some non-profit facilities for the homeless or short-term treatment centers for substance abuse, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government. The JCO can apply to buildings that are newer than October 1, 1978. The JCO can apply to a property that contains only one single-family dwelling.

rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO) - Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Evictions
rules.quote: Situations in which the property owner wishes to regain the use of the rental unit, as the result of a personal or business decision, and not the tenant's fault, may be cause for eviction, but the property owner may have to pay the tenant relocation assistance.
rules.summary: For no-fault evictions where the tenant is not at fault, property owners must pay relocation assistance to the tenant.
rules.coverage_text: In order to apply to a tenancy, it requires that the tenant either has lived in the same unit for at least six months or that their original lease expired, whichever comes first.
rules.exemption_note: No-fault reasons include: owner or immediate family member will move into the rental unit, resident manager will move into the rental unit when required by law, demolition, permanent removal from rental market, conversion to non-residential, government order to vacate, HUD owns and is selling the property, residential hotel being converted or demolished, conversion to affordable housing.

rules.title: Evictions for Non-Payment of Rent - Fair Market Rent Threshold
rules.quote: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).
rules.summary: Landlords cannot evict a tenant for non-payment of rent unless the amount owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size.
rules.effective_date_evidence: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).
rules.coverage_text: Applies to all RSO & JCO rental units.

rules.title: AB 1482 (California Tenant Protection Act of 2019) - Annual Rent Increase Cap
rules.quote: Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower
rules.summary: Annual rent increases are capped at 5% plus the regional cost of living change, or 10%, whichever is lower.
rules.coverage_text: Units that were constructed within the last 15 years (this applies on a rolling basis – i.e.. a unit constructed on January 1, 2006 is not covered as of January, 1 2020, but is covered on and after January 1, 2021).
rules.exemption_note: Exemptions include: units constructed within last 15 years (rolling), units restricted by deed to affordable housing, certain dormitories, two-unit property with owner-occupied second unit, single-family homes and condos not owned by REITs/corporations/LLCs with corporate members (if proper notice given), units already subject to RSO.

rules.title: AB 1482 (California Tenant Protection Act of 2019) - Just Cause Eviction
rules.quote: Single-family homes and condominiums are only exempt from state law but not the JCO if both (A) and (B) apply: (A) the property is not owned by one of the following: (i) a real estate trust, or (ii) a corporation, or (iii) an LLC with at least one corporate member. —–AND—- (B) The landlord notified the tenant in writing that the tenancy is not subject to the just cause and rent increase limitations
rules.summary: Single-family homes and condominiums are exempt from state just cause requirements only if not owned by a real estate trust, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, and the landlord provides written notice of the exemption to the tenant.
rules.coverage_text: Units that were constructed within the last 15 years (this applies on a rolling basis)
rules.exemption_note: Exemptions include: units constructed within last 15 years (rolling), units restricted by deed to affordable housing, certain dormitories, two-unit property with owner-occupied second unit, single-family homes and condos not owned by REITs/corporations/LLCs with corporate members (if proper notice given), units already subject to RSO.
